patch.value:
## Streaming model

- subscriptions/listen is one long-lived POST-response stream with explicit requested notification types and a server-minted subscription identifier.
- tools, prompts, resources, and resource-subscription changes flow only through the opted-in listen stream.
- progress and message notifications remain on the response stream of their originating request.
- A broken request stream loses that in-flight request and the client retries with a new JSON-RPC request id.
- STDIO and Streamable HTTP share SDK handlers, cancellation, ordering, backpressure, heartbeat policy, and structured failures.
- Streamable HTTP validates Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name and supports declared x-mcp-header parameter mappings without header injection.
MCP subscriptions and transports: subscriptions/listen, request-scoped streams, Streamable HTTP headers, retry semantics, and stdio parity
Replace connection-session and legacy subscription behavior with the 2026-07-28 long-lived listen request, request-scoped notifications, required headers, and explicit broken-stream retry semantics.

subscriptions/listen supports every specified notification type and tags notifications with the negotiated subscription id; Legacy HTTP GET, resources/subscribe, resources/unsubscribe, session headers, Last-Event-ID, SSE event ids, and redelivery semantics are absent from the canonical path; Progress and logging notifications remain request-scoped and cannot leak across concurrent requests; STDIO and Streamable HTTP pass equivalent tool, resource, prompt, cancellation, backpressure, disconnect, and retry cases; Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, and x-mcp-header behavior is schema-derived, validated, and covered against injection and mismatch
Provide standards-correct stdio and Streamable HTTP operation for request responses, opted-in changes, progress, cancellation, and disconnect recovery
Hosts can deploy pm locally or remotely with one transport-neutral state model
The revision removes HTTP GET, MCP session IDs, resource subscribe methods, SSE resumability, and Last-Event-ID while adding subscriptions/listen and required POST headers
